2884.by: Daniel Bourdeau; Claude Code session (Claude Opus 5.5), 15 Nov 2026
2884.unvetted: Not established as a cipher rather than an unidentified script. The sign side is real running text with no gloss, it is not edited in Schäfer-Shaked MTKG I-III (tables of contents of all three volumes read), and nothing published on it was found; but nobody has ruled out a known script (the Geniza holds Indian-script letters that were long unidentified: Bohak's Devanagari T-S AS 159.247-248, Fragment of the Month March 2008), and Bohak's inventory of Geniza magical fragments and the MTKG Geniza-Fragmente indices (Bd. I-III) were not opened. Next step: a palaeographer's identification (Bohak or Elbaum, Princeton Geniza Project) and the MTKG registers; if no script matches, the lead can be written open.

seen.where: CUDL IIIF, sign side MS-TS-K-00024-00024-000-00001.jp2 (native 3806 x 3664 px) viewed at 2000 x 1925 px whole, and a native-resolution region 1700,1300,1900,1500 (right half of lines 5-11 with the margin column); Arabic side MS-TS-K-00024-00024-000-00002.jp2 at 2000 x 1861 px. 15 Nov 2026.
seen.extent: One side: 11 full lines and a partial line at the torn foot, about 20-25 signs each, roughly 250 signs, with long rising strokes, dots above and below some signs and between groups; a narrow column of fainter, boxed signs down the right margin. Other side: 7 lines of large Arabic script and a row of strokes at the foot.
seen.cipher: An unidentified sign script in lines, not a row of charakteres: hooked and looped signs, some like Hebrew bet, he, het, tet, with dots. It is not the Bohak cipher of T-S K24.19 (that fragment viewed at 1600 px for comparison: a different, rounded alphabet). Nothing is written between the lines or beside them in another script, and no key or transcription is filed with it (PGP 33913: no transcription, no bibliography).

seen.extent: Recto line 11: five Greek/Coptic numeral signs after 'wa-l-'; recto line 12: three signs at the line start; verso line 5: about 11 signs (PGP: MAF reads 1, 60, 100, 400, 40, 1, 100, 1, ?, 8, 8, with doubts). About 19 signs in three words inside a Judaeo-Arabic letter.
seen.cipher: Greek/Coptic (zimam) numeral signs standing for letters, written in the line of a Judaeo-Arabic letter of Yishaq Ibn Ezra to Halfon b. Netanel; seen at native resolution on the recto with nothing written above or beside them. The letter also uses code names ('the elephant', 'the letter nun').

2885.closed: Partly read in print. Gil and Fleischer (2001) pp. 282-285 printed readings for the first two code words, ha-'marsha'at' ('the wicked woman', recto line 11) and 'tarakh' (recto line 12), by a different method for each, and none for the third (verso line 5); so reported by Friedman in India Book IV B no. 41 (H55), headnote on PGP 9097, who judges the whole matter unresolved ('tsarikh 'iyyun'). Two of three words therefore carry published, disputed proposals; the verso word has none. Gil-Fleischer's pages were not opened here, so the proposed methods are known only from Friedman's summary.

2889.by: Daniel Bourdeau; Claude Code session (Claude Opus 5.5), 15 Nov 2026
2889.unvetted: No adequate image. The Penn Museum serves only a 1600 x 1440 px frame (the EXIF shows a 5944 x 5348 px master that is not online; _2000, _2400, _3000 and other sizes return 404) in which the 8.2 cm fragment is about 520 px across, below the 1,500 px bar. At that size neither side is established as Arabic or as cipher: the labelled side has one cursive line, then a line of separate signs (strokes, a triangle, a b-like and a box-like sign) that may be Greek-Coptic numerals or fraction signs. Needs the master scan from the museum (digitalmedia@pennmuseum.org) and an Arabic papyrologist's identification; no bibliography exists.
